issues.title: Zero/negative inner-vector dimension floors elemMin at 1, leaving 24x amplification
issues.verdictReason: vectorElemMinSize's nested clause is gated on vec.Dimensions > 0, so vector<vector<float,0>,N> falls to the `size < 1 -> return 1` fallback at marshal.go:1141; I ran it: a 1 MiB payload with N=1<<20 passes the bound and reflect.MakeSlice at marshal.go:1083 allocates 25,175,696 bytes (24.0x) before the inner decoder errors.
issues.scopeReason: The amplification is identical on main (25.0x measured), but vectorElemMinSize is new code the PR added precisely to bound nested vectors, so the gap belongs in this PR.

reportedAs.anthropic-pr-review: vectorElemMinSize returns 1 whenever an inner vector's Dimensions <= 0 ... a peer can pick that number to produce a 1 MB payload that allocates 26 MB, reopening the exact DoS the bound was written to close.
reportedAs.mattpocock-review: vectorElemMinSize only adds the nested vector's size when vec.Dimensions > 0 and otherwise floors at 1 ... confirmed empirically at 24.0x amplification (25,175,696 bytes for a 1 MiB payload), defeating the PR's headline claim.
reportedAs.ce-code-review: No test covers vector<vector<float,0>,N>, the shape reaching the 'return 1' fallback; TestVectorElemMinSize pins the floor value but nothing pins what unmarshalVector then allocates for it.

issues.title: Bound counts wire bytes but allocation is Go-sized, so 16x amplification survives
issues.verdictReason: The bound divides len(data) by a wire-byte floor, but reflect.MakeSlice at marshal.go:1083 allocates info.Dimensions Go elements; I ran vector<text,1<<20> over a 1 MiB payload of zero vints into *[]string — it allocated 16,782,904 bytes (16.0x) and returned a nil error.
issues.scopeReason: Pre-existing on main, but the PR's stated purpose is to make this allocation bounded and it is the code that introduced the byte-count model.

reportedAs.ce-code-review: The bound compares Dimensions against len(data)/elemMin (wire bytes) while reflect.MakeSlice allocates using the Go element size, so a peer can still trigger allocation far larger than the payload (e.g. ~4GiB from a 256MiB body for vector<text,N>).
reportedAs.rafp-detailed: The element-count bound caps against len(data) rather than modeling per-CQL-type allocation cost, leaving up to 56x allocation amplification possible.
reportedAs.superpowers-review: Variable-length allocation amplification under the floor-of-1 is set aside as explicitly deferred or pre-existing and was not investigated in this review.

issues.title: Zero VectorType into an empty-interface destination still nil-derefs in VectorType.Zero()
issues.verdictReason: The dim-0 carve-out at marshal.go:998 keeps the bound from touching SubType, but marshal.go:1044 then calls info.Zero(), which dereferences v.SubType at marshal.go:2046; I ran `var dst any; unmarshalVector(VectorType{}, []byte{}, &dst)` on both HEAD and main and both panic with a nil pointer dereference.
issues.scopeReason: Pre-existing, but the PR's new guard comment and TestUnmarshalVectorZeroDimensionsDoesNotTouchSubType advertise this exact protection while only pinning the *[]float64 destination.

reportedAs.builtin-code-review: The new Dimensions > 0 guard prevents the bound check from dereferencing a nil SubType, but info.Zero() (via marshal.go:2046, v.SubType.NewWithError()) still panics; `var dst any; Unmarshal(VectorType{}, []byte{}, &dst)` panics with a nil-pointer dereference, verified by running it.
reportedAs.anthropic-pr-review: The comment says the dim-0 carve-out exists so a caller-supplied zero VectorType cannot panic on the Scan goroutine, but the table only uses `var dst []float64`, which never touches SubType; with `var dst any` both rows still panic.
reportedAs.rafp-review: The bound is skipped at Dimensions == 0 so a nil SubType cannot panic there, and a test asserts this, but the generic path then calls info.Zero(), which dereferences v.SubType unconditionally.

issues.title: vectorElemMinSize(nil) panics when Dimensions > 0 despite the guard's nil-SubType claim
issues.verdictReason: vectorElemMinSize calls vectorFixedElemSize(elemType), which calls elemType.Type() on the nil interface; VectorType{Dimensions: 3, SubType: nil} with non-nil data reaches it. On main the fast-path switch did info.SubType.Type() behind the identical guard, so it is exact parity, not a regression.
issues.scopeReason: The PR's own comment at marshal.go:995-997 reasons about caller-supplied nil SubTypes, so the incomplete invariant belongs with the code that states it.

reportedAs.rafp-detailed: The new guard's comment claims it protects against a nil SubType, but it only covers the Dimensions == 0 case; with Dimensions > 0 and non-nil data, vectorElemMinSize(nil) still panics via nil.Type().
reportedAs.tob-diff-review: unmarshalVector(VectorType{Dimensions: 3}, make([]byte,12), &dst) still nil-derefs in vectorFixedElemSize; the guard adds a second, earlier copy of the dereference under a comment that reads as if it were handled.
reportedAs.ce-code-review: With Dimensions > 0 and non-nil data, a caller-constructed VectorType with a nil SubType reaches vectorFixedElemSize(nil) and panics calling Type() on a nil interface; pre-existing.
reportedAs.superpowers-review: vectorElemMinSize nil-derefs on a nil SubType when Dimensions>0; not a regression (exact parity with the old fast path) and unreachable from the wire.

issues.title: Nested vector inner type keeps the bare VectorType prefix, so the new error names nothing
issues.verdictReason: helpers.go:271 builds the VectorType's NativeType from prefix+"VectorType" rather than the parsed `name`; I ran Unmarshal of a wire-parsed vector<vector<float,3>,2> into *any and got exactly `unmarshal vector: no Go type for element type custom(org.apache.cassandra.db.marshal.VectorType)` — no element type, no dimension.
issues.scopeReason: The PR's stated goal for the sibling branch is that the error say what the server sent, and the same one-line fix in the function it edits would deliver it here.

reportedAs.anthropic-pr-review: NewCustomType(protoVer, TypeCustom, prefix+"VectorType") stores the bare prefix, so the PR's new error for a nested vector reads with no element type or dimension; storing `name` there instead would fix both the message and nested-vector decoding into interface{}.
reportedAs.builtin-code-review: This branch still stores prefix+"VectorType" without the parenthesized subtype, so asVectorType cannot parse it, NewWithError fails, Zero() returns nil, and a nested-vector column errors out of MapScan/Scan(&any) with an unhelpful message.
reportedAs.rafp-detailed: The VectorType branch still calls NewCustomType with just the prefix instead of the full name, so nested vector types resolve to a bare custom() type with no Go type.
reportedAs.ce-code-review: For a nested vector, the new guard prints the bare prefix 'no Go type for element type custom(...)' because getCassandraLongType builds the nested VectorType's NativeType from a constant prefix rather than the parsed spec.
reportedAs.mattpocock-review: helpers.go:280-284 only fixes the unknown-basic-type case; the inner VectorType still carries the bare custom name and has no String(), so the nested-vector error path prints 'no Go type for element type custom(...VectorType)' without element type or dimensions.
reportedAs.tob-diff-review: For the nested-vector case, the message still reports custom(org.apache.cassandra.db.marshal.VectorType) with no element type or dimensions, because the inner type is built with prefix+"VectorType" rather than name.
reportedAs.superpowers-review: VectorType has no String(), so %v falls through to the promoted NativeType.String() and the error reads 'no Go type for element type custom(...VectorType)' with no element type or dimension.

issues.title: Saturation branch `return math.MaxInt32` in vectorElemMinSize has zero test coverage
issues.verdictReason: I ran the full `-tags unit` suite with -coverprofile: block marshal.go:1136.55,1138.4 reports 0 executions while every other block in vectorElemMinSize is covered. It is the only new arithmetic in the diff left unpinned.
issues.scopeReason: The branch is new code added by this PR.

reportedAs.anthropic-pr-review: vectorElemMinSize measures 92.3% coverage; the uncovered block is exactly `return math.MaxInt32`, the subtlest new line guarding a peer-supplied inner dimension.
reportedAs.ce-code-review: The saturation branch in vectorElemMinSize guarding against a nested peer-controlled Dimensions overflow is never exercised by any test, so a bug in the comparison, boundary, or int64-to-int narrowing there would go uncaught.
reportedAs.rafp-detailed: mutation testing shows replacing it with 'return 1' leaves the suite green, unlike every other guard the diff adds.
reportedAs.rafp-review: Coverage profile reports zero executions for the saturation guard at marshal.go:1136-1138.
reportedAs.superpowers-review: The `return math.MaxInt32` overflow-saturation branch shows 0 hits in the coverage profile while every other block in vectorElemMinSize is covered; it is wire-reachable.
reportedAs.tob-diff-review: The saturation branch is the only overflow guard in the new arithmetic, but TestVectorElemMinSize only covers 0 and -3 dimensions.

issues.title: Zero-length variable-length elements still decode to garbage with a nil error
issues.verdictReason: vectorElemMinSize returns 1 for every variable-length type, below their real wire minimum; I ran vector<date,3> over []byte{0,0,0} and got ["-5877641-06-23" x3] with nil error, and vector<smallint,3> over the same payload gave [0 0 0] with nil error.
issues.scopeReason: Identical on main; the PR's bound is an allocation guard, not element validation, and it does not make this reachable or worse.

reportedAs.ce-code-review: Zero-length date/time elements pass the new bound and still allocate one Go value per claimed element, decoding to minDate with a nil error instead of being rejected.
reportedAs.anthropic-pr-review: For every variable-length type vectorElemMinSize returns 1 regardless of body, so a vector<smallint,4> can still decode a short/zero-length payload to garbage values instead of erroring; the description's claim that such payloads now error is true only for fixed-size elements.

issues.title: VectorType.Zero() discards NewWithError's error, so the new message cannot name the cause
issues.verdictReason: marshal.go:2046-2049 returns nil on any error from v.SubType.NewWithError() without propagating `e`, so the new error at marshal.go:1048 can only print the type, not why it has no Go representation.
issues.scopeReason: The error message that cannot name the cause is new in this PR.

reportedAs.anthropic-pr-review: VectorType.Zero() drops the underlying error `e`; the real cause is that VectorType never overrides NewWithError, but the guard reports a misleading message.
reportedAs.builtin-code-review: VectorType.Zero() discards the error returned by NewWithError, so the new error message at marshal.go:1048 can only name the type and not the reason for the failure.

issues.title: Identical `info.Dimensions > 0 && data != nil` guard appears twice back to back
issues.verdictReason: marshal.go:998 and marshal.go:1007 are byte-identical conditions with different bodies and separate comment blocks; merging them is behaviour-preserving since the bound has no early return that the fast paths depend on ordering for.
issues.scopeReason: The duplicate guard is the block this PR added.

reportedAs.anthropic-pr-review: The identical `info.Dimensions > 0 && data != nil` check appears at both marshal.go:998 and marshal.go:1007 and should be merged into one block.
reportedAs.mattpocock-review: marshal.go:996 and marshal.go:1005 both contain 'if info.Dimensions > 0 && data != nil {' back to back with different bodies and separate explanatory comments; the repetition is the first thing a reader trips on.

issues.title: getCassandraLongType indexes split results unguarded, panicking on a malformed type name
issues.verdictReason: names[1] at helpers.go:264 and make([]UDTField, len(names)-2) at helpers.go:243 have no arity check, unlike the MapType branch at helpers.go:224; I ran getCassandraLongType on "...VectorType(...FloatType)", "...VectorType()" and bare "...VectorType" and all three panic with index out of range [1] with length 1, on both HEAD and main.
issues.scopeReason: Pre-existing in branches this diff does not touch; the PR only edits the trailing basic-type else branch.

reportedAs.rafp-detailed: names[1], make([]UDTField, len(names)-2), and spec[1] are indexed without checking the split produced enough parts, causing index-out-of-range or negative-length-slice panics reachable through framer.readTypeInfo; the sibling MapType branch guards the same pattern.
reportedAs.rafp-review: splitJavaCompositeTypes' result is indexed without a length check; a peer-supplied malformed type name causes an index-out-of-range or makeslice len-out-of-range panic. parseFrame's recover re-panics runtime.Error, killing the read goroutine and the process.
reportedAs.anthropic-pr-review: names[1] panics with an index-out-of-range error on a truncated vector spec such as ...VectorType(...FloatType); it's reachable via asVectorType → goType → NewWithError → Iter.Scan, which is unrecovered.
reportedAs.ce-code-review: helpers.go:264 indexes names[1] unguarded; a malformed name from the wire panics there. Pre-existing and unchanged.
reportedAs.superpowers-review: A parseFrame-recovered slicing panic at helpers.go:265 is set aside as explicitly deferred or pre-existing.

issues.title: readTypeInfo slices the vector custom name unchecked, panicking on the frame goroutine
issues.verdictReason: frame.go:856 does spec[1:len(spec)-1] and frame.go:858-859 index spec[:idx] with an unchecked LastIndex result; I ran readTypeInfo over custom names "...VectorType", "...VectorTypeX", "...VectorType()" and "...VectorType(...FloatType)" and all four panic with slice bounds out of range. parseFrame at frame.go:474 re-panics runtime.Error, so the process dies.
issues.scopeReason: Pre-existing and entirely untouched by this diff.

reportedAs.rafp-detailed: readTypeInfo assumes the custom type spec has a trailing ) and a comma when slicing, so names like ...VectorType, ...VectorType(), or malformed variants cause 'slice bounds out of range' panics on the connection goroutine.
reportedAs.rafp-review: readTypeInfo slices a vector custom-type string blind; inputs like ...VectorType, ...VectorTypeX, ...VectorType(...FloatType) all panic through parseFrame.
reportedAs.ce-code-review: frame.go does spec[1:len(spec)-1] and spec[:idx] where idx may be -1; a malformed name from the wire panics there.
reportedAs.superpowers-review: A parseFrame-recovered slicing panic at frame.go:855-857 is set aside as explicitly deferred or pre-existing.

issues.title: readBytes slices p[:size] with an unchecked peer-supplied length
issues.verdictReason: readBytes at marshal.go:1565-1570 rejects only size < 0 and then does p[:size]; I ran Unmarshal of a tuple<int> over []byte{0x7f,0xff,0xff,0xff} and got a panic: slice bounds out of range [:2147483647] with capacity 0, on the Scan goroutine where nothing recovers.
issues.scopeReason: Pre-existing tuple/UDT code untouched by this vector-focused diff.

reportedAs.rafp-detailed: readBytes performs p[:size] using an attacker/server-controlled size with no bounds check, so a malformed length in any UDT field or tuple element panics on the Scan goroutine with no recover.
reportedAs.rafp-review: readBytes trusts the peer's element length, causing a slice-bounds panic in unmarshalUDT/unmarshalTuple on Scan's goroutine.

issues.title: unmarshalTuple calls reflect.Set without an assignability check and panics
issues.verdictReason: marshal.go:1631/1636 Set decoded values into destination fields with no AssignableTo check; I ran Unmarshal of tuple<int,text> into *[]float32 and got a panic: reflect.Set: value of type int is not assignable to type float32.
issues.scopeReason: Pre-existing tuple code the diff does not touch.

reportedAs.rafp-detailed: unmarshalTuple performs reflect.Set without checking assignability, so e.g. vector<tuple<int,text>,2> into *[][]float32 panics with 'value of type int is not assignable to type float32' instead of returning an unmarshal error.
reportedAs.rafp-review: unmarshalTuple panics instead of returning an error on a mismatched or unexported destination field.

issues.title: scanColumn returns 1 for a nil tuple destination, silently dropping every later column
issues.verdictReason: session.go:2974-2976 returns 1 whenever dest[0] == nil, before the TypeTuple branch at session.go:2978 that would return len(tuple.Elems); passing nil to skip a tuple column therefore misaligns every subsequent destination while Scan still reports success.
issues.scopeReason: Pre-existing scan plumbing unrelated to the vector changes.

reportedAs.rafp-review: Passing nil to skip a tuple column returns 1 instead of len(Elems), silently dropping every later column; Scan still returns true with nil error.

issues.title: vectorSliceReuse aliases one backing array across rows for float/double vectors

reportedAs.rafp-review: vectorSliceReuse aliases one backing array across rows for vector<float> and vector<double> only (introduced in commit f42df61).

issues.title: getCassandraLongType parse cost is super-linear in nested type-name length (52s at 37 KB)
issues.verdictReason: I timed getCassandraLongType over synthetic nested vector names: 4.7 KB took 147 ms, 18.8 KB took 9.1 s and 37.6 KB took 52.3 s, all on the frame-parsing goroutine, and a wire custom name may be up to 65535 bytes. The finding's specific 98-byte / 80-second reproduction did not replicate (17 microseconds).
issues.scopeReason: Pre-existing parse behaviour untouched by this diff.

reportedAs.rafp-detailed: One reviewer reproduced an 80s+ hang with a 98-byte custom name causing thousands of recursive frames in getCassandraLongType, but a follow-up reconciler could not reproduce it on the same commit.
reportedAs.tob-diff-review: dwarfed by a pre-existing quadratic type-name parse (38s for the same name).

issues.title: frame.go discards strconv.Atoi's error for the vector dimension
issues.verdictReason: frame.go:861 is `dim, _ := strconv.Atoi(...)`, so a non-numeric dimension becomes 0 and an overflowing one becomes MaxInt with ErrRange dropped; the operator then sees a downstream vector error rather than the real parse failure. helpers.go:265 does log and degrade for the same parse.
issues.scopeReason: Pre-existing line the diff does not touch.

reportedAs.anthropic-pr-review: frame.go:861 discards ErrRange from strconv.Atoi, so an overflowing dimension becomes MaxInt64 and the operator never learns what string the server actually sent.
reportedAs.rafp-detailed: The error from parsing the vector dimension via strconv.Atoi is discarded, so a non-numeric dimension silently becomes 0 and an out-of-range one becomes MaxInt64, producing a misleading 'N bytes of data for 0-dimension vector' error.

issues.title: Other getCassandraLongType degrade paths still return a nameless custom type
issues.verdictReason: helpers.go:224 (map arity) and helpers.go:266 (vector dim parse) both return NewNativeType(protoVer, TypeCustom) with no name; I ran the map-arity case and got NativeType{custom:"", typ:custom}, now inconsistent with the named degrade the PR added at helpers.go:280-283.
issues.scopeReason: The PR created the inconsistency by naming one degrade path in the same function and leaving its siblings nameless.

reportedAs.rafp-review: Only the unknown-basic-type branch keeps the name; map-arity failure and vector dimension-parse failure return NewNativeType(protoVer, TypeCustom) with no name, so the nested-vector case still reports custom(org.apache.cassandra.db.marshal.VectorType).
reportedAs.anthropic-pr-review: helpers.go:222/267 still degrade to a nameless custom() on parse failure, now inconsistent with the change at helpers.go:279.

issues.title: Zero-dimension inner vector now errors on a payload that decoded on base
issues.verdictReason: The 1-byte fallback at marshal.go:1141 is stricter than the wire format, which encodes vector<vector<int,0>,N> in zero bytes (the inner vector classifies fixed-length, so no prefix is written). I ran it: main decodes an empty payload to [[] [] []] with nil error, HEAD returns "3 dimensions do not fit in 0 bytes".
issues.scopeReason: The behaviour change is created by the new bound and is not listed among the PR body's behaviour changes.

reportedAs.superpowers-review: vector<vector<int,0>,3> over an empty payload decoded to [[] [] []] on base but now errors '3 dimensions do not fit in 0 bytes' because the minimum-size floor is 1 byte while the true wire size is 0; a third unlisted behaviour change.
reportedAs.anthropic-pr-review: The unconditional claim is false because vector<vector<float,0>,N> encodes to zero bytes and the bound does narrow there, making the statement degenerate but still incorrect as written.

issues.title: Negative dimensions on a NULL payload now error instead of returning nil, undocumented
issues.verdictReason: The new check at marshal.go:992 runs before the data == nil branch at marshal.go:1053; I ran unmarshalVector(vector<float,-3>, nil, &dst) on main (nil error, dst nil) and on HEAD ("negative dimensions -3"). It is deliberate and test-pinned but absent from the description's behaviour-change paragraph.
issues.scopeReason: The reordering is this PR's.

reportedAs.superpowers-review: Base code returned nil for negative dimensions on a NULL payload because the data==nil branch ran first; the new code now errors instead — deliberate, test-pinned, and arguably better, but a behaviour change absent from the description's list.

issues.title: Non-NULL zero-length payloads now error, breaking driver-produced round-trips
issues.verdictReason: The PR documents the vector<int,3>-over-empty case, but the same bound also rejects what marshalVector itself emits: I marshalled []*int32{nil,nil} for vector<int,2>, got 0 bytes with a nil error, and unmarshalling it back now fails with "2 dimensions do not fit in 0 bytes". Only vector<int,3> is table-tested.
issues.scopeReason: The bound is new and the affected shapes are untested.

reportedAs.builtin-code-review: The documented behavior change is correct but is a visible API break for anyone who relied on a non-NULL zero-length payload with Dimensions > 0 decoding to zero values instead of erroring.
reportedAs.ce-code-review: The new bound rejects every payload marshalVector produces for a fixed-size element encoded in zero bytes (nil pointers, zero time.Time, UnsetValue), flipping from silent zero-filled decode to an error; also, no table test round-trips Marshal then Unmarshal over those shapes.

issues.title: marshalVector emits a wire-invalid value when an element under-marshals
issues.verdictReason: I marshalled []*int32{nil,nil} into vector<int,2> and []time.Time{{},{}} into vector<timestamp,2>: both return 0 bytes with a nil error, a value no server will accept for a 2-element fixed-length vector.
issues.scopeReason: Pre-existing marshal-side behaviour untouched by this diff.

reportedAs.ce-code-review: marshalVector writes bytes with no prefix and no length check when an element (nil pointer, UnsetValue, or zero time.Time) marshals to fewer bytes than vectorFixedElemSize, producing a wire-invalid value the caller only learns about via the server's InvalidRequest.

issues.title: Allocation test asserts on process-global TotalAlloc with a payload-relative budget
issues.verdictReason: marshal_vector_test.go:846-855 reads runtime.MemStats.TotalAlloc, which is process-wide, and compares against payload/8 (128 KB) rather than an absolute figure; omitting t.Parallel() keeps sibling subtests out but not the package's background dialers and loggers. The ~3.5 KB actual against 128 KB headroom is what carries it.
issues.scopeReason: The test is new in this PR.

reportedAs.rafp-review: The test's allocation assertion measures process-global TotalAlloc; it caught the prior regression and never flaked, so tightening it is deferred as not worth doing now.
reportedAs.superpowers-review: The allocation assertion reads process-global runtime.TotalAlloc; held under -count=5, -shuffle=on with 128KB headroom against ~3.5KB actual, but the 'not parallel' comment only covers sibling subtests, not the suite's background dialers/loggers.
reportedAs.anthropic-pr-review: The payload/8 budget is coupled to payload against ~3 KB of fixed overhead, so below ~32 KB the test fails for unrelated reasons; an absolute budget would be sturdier.

issues.title: Allocation-bound test covers only the nested fixed-size shape, not variable-length

issues.title: No dimension-bound test goes through the public Unmarshal or Scan with a wire-parsed type

issues.title: Dimension-bound error message names neither the element type nor the per-element minimum
issues.verdictReason: The message at marshal.go:1001 prints only Dimensions and len(data), while the fast-path messages it preempts print the exact expected byte count and the type is available as info.SubType. Cosmetic: the message already names both peer-controlled numbers.
issues.scopeReason: The message is new in this PR.

reportedAs.anthropic-pr-review: A short payload's error loses the exact byte count ("3 dimensions do not fit in 4 bytes") while a surplus payload's error keeps it ("expected 12 bytes, got 16"); including elemMin in the message would restore the arithmetic symmetry.
reportedAs.ce-code-review: The new dimension-bound error omits info.SubType, unlike the fast-path errors it preempts.

issues.title: VectorType.Zero() yields []*T while goType() yields []T, so Scan(&any) and MapScan differ
issues.verdictReason: marshal.go:2050 does SliceOf(TypeOf(t)) where t is the pointer NewWithError returns, while helpers.go:147-149 strips the pointer; I ran Unmarshal of a wire vector<float,3> into *any and got []*float32, and the new test at marshal_vector_test.go:919 asserts exactly that, freezing the inconsistency.
issues.scopeReason: Pre-existing in Zero(), but the PR's new test pins the inconsistent shape and the new guard could have used goType(info) instead.

reportedAs.tob-diff-review: reflect.TypeOf(info.Zero()) yields []*T while goType() (used by unmarshalList and reached via MapScan) yields []T; Scan(&any) gives []*float32 but MapScan gives []float32 for vector<float,3>, and the test at marshal_vector_test.go:928 freezes this inconsistency.
reportedAs.superpowers-review: VectorType.Zero() yielding []*T is set aside as explicitly deferred or pre-existing.

reportedAs.mattpocock-review: helpers.go:280-284 changes what getCassandraLongType returns for an unrecognised basic type, which leaks into every TypeInfo consumer's String()/error text, but has no godoc.

issues.title: vectorElemMinSize is recomputed for every value with cost quadratic in nesting depth
issues.verdictReason: The call at marshal.go:999 runs unconditionally per value and walks the whole SubType chain; I measured 334 microseconds for a 200-deep nested type. Real but negligible: the same type's one-time getCassandraLongType parse takes 788 ms, and flat vector benchmarks show no regression.
issues.scopeReason: The per-value call is new in this PR.

reportedAs.tob-diff-review: vectorElemMinSize is recomputed per value with quadratic cost relative to depth, measured at 2.7ms per 4-byte value for an 800-deep type.
reportedAs.ce-code-review: unmarshalVector now calls vectorElemMinSize(info.SubType) unconditionally ahead of the float fast paths and recomputes it every row uncached; benchmarks show head and base indistinguishable within noise.

issues.title: Deferred #1106: oversized vint element length narrows to -1, decoding empty with nil error
issues.verdictReason: marshal.go:1097 does elemSize = int(m) from readUnsignedVInt, and the `elemSize >= 0` guard at marshal.go:1104 then skips consuming any bytes when the conversion goes negative, leaving unmarshalData nil and the element decoding as empty with a nil error.
issues.scopeReason: Pre-existing and explicitly deferred by the PR description; the new bound does not make it reachable or worse.

reportedAs.ce-code-review: With the one-byte floor letting variable-length vectors through, a max-width VInt element length converts via int(m) to -1, so no payload bytes are consumed and the element silently decodes as an empty string with a nil error.
reportedAs.anthropic-pr-review: vint length narrowing to negative makes vector<text,1> decode [""] with nil error; reachable as described but correctly scoped out of this PR.
reportedAs.superpowers-review: The vint-narrowing-to-negative path (#1106) is set aside as explicitly deferred or pre-existing.

issues.title: Deferred #1086: surplus trailing bytes dropped on the generic path, rejected on fast paths
issues.verdictReason: The generic loop at marshal.go:1095-1116 consumes exactly Dimensions elements and never checks for leftover data, while the float fast paths at marshal.go:1012 and 1027 require len(data) == expected; the PR's own test 'payload with a trailing byte' pins the asymmetry.
issues.scopeReason: Pre-existing and explicitly deferred by the PR description.

reportedAs.anthropic-pr-review: surplus trailing bytes silently dropped in the generic path while fast paths reject them; reachable as described but correctly scoped out of this PR.
reportedAs.ce-code-review: Surplus trailing bytes in a generic (non-float-fast-path) vector payload are still accepted rather than rejected, unlike the float fast paths which reject the same malformed payload.
reportedAs.superpowers-review: Trailing-byte distribution (#1086) is set aside as explicitly deferred or pre-existing.

issues.title: Peer-controlled type descriptor text reaches error messages verbatim
